question: An if-statement is used to execute a block of code only if a specified condition evaluates to True.
In an if-statement, the condition must be an integer for the statement to work properly.
An else clause is required in an if-statement.
An if-statement can evaluate multiple conditions using the 'and' keyword.
If an if-statement condition evaluates to False, the code block within that if-statement will still execute.
You can nest if-statements within each other to create more complex decision-making structures.
In Python, an if-statement can directly evaluate the value of a string to determine if it is True or False.
An if-statement can have several elif clauses, but only one else clause.
When using multiple if-statements sequentially, both can execute even if the first condition evaluates to True.
An if-statement can only compare numerical data types and cannot be used with booleans or strings.
